the southern Mendered Massif comprises two distinct types (i.e. ‘core’ and ‘cover’) of granitoid bodies, which were emplaced in a top-to-the-SSW extensional ductile shear zone during the Late Oligocene.
the Menderes metamorphic core complex comprises a complex assemblage of rocks that are not only deformed and metamophosed during Alpine orogeny but also intruded by Tertiary granites.
the granitoid bodies of the ‘core of the southern Menders Massif’ are Tertiary in age and are not related to the Alpine orogeny.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no ‘core of the Menderess Massif’ in the sense of an undeformed, unmetamorphosed granitoid basement.
the Menderes core is a heterogeneous assemblage of granitoid bodies, which were emplaced in a ductile extension setting.
the Menderes Metamorphic Core Complex (MMCC), as a whole, is not a monolithic unit.
